topic: Zeeland Energy Terminal (ZET) — 2025/26 development status, FID timeline, FSRU and operator detail
wiki_text: The Zeeland Energy Terminal (ZET), proposed by VTTI and Höegh Evi (formerly Höegh LNG), advanced through 2025–2026 as a Dutch LNG import project. An open season opened with an Expression of Interest phase that closed 6 March 2026, with the broader commercial process expected to conclude by end-2026. A final investment decision is expected by Q3 2027, with commercial operations targeted for late 2029 / Q4 2029. The FSRU-based terminal would be located in the harbour of Vlissingen-Oost (Zeeland province, as GEM already records), with approximately 7.5 billion m3/y of send-out capacity and at least 180,000 m3 of LNG storage, and would be the first privately operated LNG import terminal in the Netherlands. Höegh Evi is consistently described as the FSRU/vessel provider and a co-developer/co-operator; no specific FSRU vessel has been publicly named for the terminal as of June 2026 (a reason GEM's FloatingVesselName and Operator fields are left blank rather than populated). VTTI's parents per GEM remain ADNOC, IFM Investors and Vitol Holding II SA.
source_notes: Re-sourced per reverify brief to independent non-GEM trade press. Core claims corroborated across >=2 independent outlets: late 2029 / Q4 2029 start (LNG Industry, World-Energy, Hydrocarbon Engineering — all verified to contain '2029'); FID Q3 2027 (World-Energy verified '2027'); ~7.5 billion m3/y send-out (LNG Industry, Hydrocarbon Engineering, Tanks and Terminals — all verified '7.5'); first privately operated Dutch LNG import terminal (World-Energy). The precise '180,000 m3' storage figure verifies on the official project site zeelandenergyterminal.com (trade press uses 'at least 180,000'); independent outlets confirm an LNG-storage FSRU design. No GEM-published URLs used as citations.
